args.rationale:
Successor liability screening for ACQUISITION 2 (Dunlow Cold Storage asset purchase / vendor invoice demand). Under the general rule, an asset purchaser is not liable for the seller's debts and liabilities unless one of four exceptions applies. Applying the firm memo's framework:

1. EXPRESS AGREEMENT — NOT APPLICABLE: The Dunlow purchase agreement contains NO assumption of liabilities of any kind. There is no assumption clause covering the vendor invoice class, so this exception yields nothing.

2. FRAUDULENT CONVEYANCE — NOT APPLICABLE: The sale was arm's-length and the price was certified by Halcyon's banker as fair market value. Per Section 3(b), payment of fair market value in an arm's-length sale negates the fraudulent conveyance indicators. There is no inadequate consideration, no seller left insolvent to strand known claims, and no awareness of looming claims driving the structure.

3. DE FACTO MERGER — NOT APPLICABLE: A de facto merger requires continuity of ownership between seller shareholders and purchaser, cessation/dissolution of the seller, assumption of operations needed to continue the business, and continuity of management. Here, Dunlow remained in existence after closing, retained its corporate registration, and applied sale proceeds to its creditors. Per Section 3(c), seller survival with retained separate existence defeats de facto merger. There is also no continuity of ownership or management (no shared officers, directors, or shareholders). This exception does not apply.

4. MERE CONTINUATION — NOT APPLICABLE: Mere continuation requires common officers, directors, or shareholders with only one corporation remaining after the transfer. No officer, director, or shareholder of Dunlow holds any position or share in Halcyon, and Halcyon has never held itself out as Dunlow. Per Section 3(d), absence of any shared officers/directors/shareholders defeats mere continuation, and Dunlow did not cease to exist (two corporations remain). This exception does not apply.

The transaction bears all of the features of (b), (c), and (d) under Section 3, with no assumption clause. The vendor's mere unpaid invoice against Dunlow does not trigger any exception — the general rule controls, and the purchaser (Halcyon) takes free of Dunlow's liabilities. Successor exposure does NOT attach. Determination: REJECTED.
